    Troubleshooting

    Device doesn't appear in the list

    • Make sure your computer and the device are on the same Wi-Fi network. Guest networks or networks that block device-to-device traffic may prevent discovery.
    • Make sure Wireless debugging is on. It can turn off when the device locks or changes networks.
    • Make sure the device runs Android 11 or newer. See Requirements.

    Device name or API shows "—"

    If the serial number appears in place of the device name and ADB Wi-Fi and API show "—", the adb server that's currently running is an older version. Check the note at the bottom of the window and fix it based on the cause.

    An update notice for Platform-Tools also appears

    Platform-Tools in Unity's Android SDK is below 37. Install the latest version with Update Platform-Tools. The adb server is restarted with the new version when the install finishes.

    Only "The running adb server is an older version" appears

    Unity's adb is up to date, but another program (scrcpy, Homebrew adb, an older Android Studio SDK, etc.) started the server first with an older adb.

    1. Click Restart adb Server at the bottom and confirm with Restart. The server is stopped and started again with the newest installed adb.

      • Other tools using adb, such as Android Studio or Logcat, briefly lose their connection.
      • Running adb kill-server in a terminal does the same. The window starts the server again with the newest adb shortly after.

    2. If "Another program started an older adb server again" appears after restarting, that program keeps relaunching the server. Find out which adb it is, then update that program or point it at the same Android SDK.

      macOS:

      lsof -nP -iTCP:5037 -sTCP:LISTEN

      Use the PID from the output to find the executable path.

      ps -p <PID> -o comm=

      Windows (Command Prompt):

      netstat -ano | findstr :5037

      Find the PID in the last column on the Details tab of Task Manager, then right-click > Open file location.

    "Can't reach the adb server"

    The window connects to the running adb server (127.0.0.1:5037 by default) to find devices. If the server doesn't respond, it starts one with the newest installed adb.

    • If it still can't connect, click Open Preferences… and set the adb path yourself.
    • Make sure a firewall or security software isn't blocking adb.

    List briefly empties or the connection drops

    This can happen when Unity and another tool (such as Android Studio) keep stopping and restarting each other's adb server.

    • If Preferences > External Tools > Kill external ADB instances is on, Unity stops adb servers that aren't from its own SDK. Turn it off if you use other tools at the same time.
    • If Unity's SDK and the other tool use different Platform-Tools versions, they restart each other's server. Update Unity's SDK, or point Preferences > External Tools > Android SDK at the same SDK.

    "Android Build Support isn't installed"

    Add the Android Build Support module to your editor version in Unity Hub, then restart the editor.
